title: Fictional matter docket and deadline tracker

parent.objective: Maintain a source-pinned docket and deadline index for the fictional Doe v. Doe matter so every downstream workstream cites a stable procedural baseline.
parent.milestone: Docket baseline complete and deadline arithmetic verified

goal: Build a chronological docket index from the fictional filing manifest and verify every computed deadline against its triggering event and the applicable rule.
non_goals: Advise on strategy, relief, or admissibility.
File, serve, or change any real case record.

allowed: Index the embedded fictional filing manifest.
Compute and check deadline arithmetic against the manifest's stated rule periods.
prohibited: Introduce real people, cases, court orders, or legal authorities.
Assert case facts beyond the filing manifest's own labels.

inputs.name: Fictional filing manifest
inputs.description: FAM10-DKT-001: fictional complaint filed 2026-01-06; FAM10-DKT-002: fictional answer filed 2026-01-27; FAM10-DKT-003: fictional temporary custody order entered 2026-02-10. All fictional; establish no real case fact.

outputs.name: Docket index
outputs.description: Chronological rows with docket id, event, date, and triggering rule period where applicable.

outputs.name: Deadline verification record
outputs.description: Recomputed deadline for each triggering event compared against the manifest's stated value.

interface.name: fictional_docket_index
interface.description: Input filing manifest; output index rows and a deadline-arithmetic verification record.

assumptions: All manifest entries are invented solely for this worked example.
Filing date order determines index order.

sources.reference: The three fictional filing entries embedded in this contract's inputs.
sources.authority: Synthetic fixture manifest only; no real docket or court record.

acceptance_criteria.description: The index contains exactly one row for each manifest entry, in filing-date order.
Every recomputed deadline matches the manifest's stated triggering rule period exactly.

validation.description: Recompute the index from the manifest and check row count and ordering.
evidence_required: Manifest-to-index comparison with row count and ordering.

argv: manifest = [('FAM10-DKT-001', '2026-01-06'), ('FAM10-DKT-002', '2026-01-27'), ('FAM10-DKT-003', '2026-02-10')]; ordered = sorted(manifest, key=lambda row: row[1]); assert ordered == manifest and len(ordered) == 3; print('docket index stable')

validation.description: Recompute the answer deadline (21 days from complaint filing) and check it against the manifest.
evidence_required: Recomputed date compared to the manifest's stated filing date for the answer.

argv: import datetime; filed = datetime.date(2026, 1, 6); due = filed + datetime.timedelta(days=21); answered = datetime.date(2026, 1, 27); assert due == answered, (due, answered); print('deadline arithmetic verified')

context_scope: This contract and the embedded fictional filing manifest.
The derived docket index and its deadline verification record.
architecture_boundaries: Keep originals distinct from the derived index.
Make no legal determination and perform no external writes.
